page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-24GB is a Cloud Native virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 shared x86_64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 24.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile. Single-core CPU performance is limited, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 6254.7 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9153.0. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth reaches an average of 821.2 GB/sec, the Passmark memory score is weak, falling into the bottom 25%. LLM inference speeds are average for small 135M models but drop to poor levels for medium 7B models.

Given its shared CPU allocation and lack of dedicated local storage, this server offers a cost-efficient entry point for multi-threaded workloads that do not require sustained, high-frequency single-core performance. The resource density of 24.0 GB RAM alongside 8 shared cores makes it suitable for general-purpose tasks, multi-threaded decompression, and moderate database operations, while it is less suited for high-throughput static web serving or intensive LLM inference.
